implementation_notes: Default .NET realization on a cloud broker: the subscription is a durable virtual queue per subscriber, with rules/filters replacing the classic subscription registry and Complete/Abandon replacing acknowledgement. Choose it when the platform is Azure and the same namespace should own retention, TTL and dead-lettering.
pitfalls: Deleting a subscription deletes its backlog; renaming it silently starts from zero.
Default message TTL (14 days) limits how long a subscriber may be offline.

variants.name: Kafka consumer group with manual offset commit (Confluent.Kafka)
variants.implementation_notes: Where Kafka is the broker, the group id names the durable subscription and the committed offset is the retained position, bounded by offset and topic retention. Choose it when the same log feeds several consumers and the replay window should be shared with other systems.
pitfalls: Auto-commit enabled by default in many samples commits before processing; disable it or accept the loss window.
AutoOffsetReset=Latest skips the accumulated backlog when no committed offset exists.
